author: Ifmyante
text:
From a different journal:

bobyv87 wrote: IF, i still dont
understand why is so much stress to double or triple a account each
month if you said you used to risk 5% /trade and you used to take 10 or
15 R trades. and you said also that you can find a few trades on each
week. From what i understand you dont neet too many trades with 5% risk
and 10 R to reach your goal monthly. I have also seen a retailer who
managed to make, i dont know how 1000% for two months in a row with many
 many trades. If retailer can do that, i dont know if it should be so
complicated for a RTMer. P.S. I see also Salivan's equity curve and in i
 think 60 trades he only loses 2 in a row. With this in mind, i think
you can risk even 10%/trade and still be good. How difficult is to have 4
 profitable trades in a row with 10:1?
Ifmyante wrote: You're in an uncomfortable place, for sure, and you're neither the first nor the last to be there.

The ideal RTM student is already set up, living off grid, with a part time job doing some work in nature.

His family have everything they need to survive for the next few years, and there's no need to become a master in an hurry.

In your situation, you have a deadline. Sure, it's prudent to have one,
but such a short deadline to master perhaps the most difficult
discipline there is, can only be detrimental to your progress.

The pressure on you to perform, while the bank balance is forever
shrinking, and you see your loved ones trying to be patient, is immense!

Sure, some people get to be consistently profitable in six months, but for the majority it's going to take three years.

I see where you're up to in your learning, and I know that you can make
it. But you'll need to give yourself a real, stress free, chance to do
so.

The mind does a lot of processing while you're engaged in menial tasks,
making a part time job a great advantage for anybody learning the
markets.

I feel for you brother. At the start of RTM, I made myself homeless,
leaving everything behind, and for the first six months I had to double
or triple my account every month just to make ends meet. So I know the
stress you're under.

I can't ask you to keep at it, but I can say that you have a great chance of success if you find a way to earn while you learn

There's a massive difference between trading to add to your wealth, and trading to survive.

NEEDING the wins by a certain date puts massive pressure on any trader.

We don't mind if it takes an extra month to earn a nice supercar, but we mind very much a month between meals.
